grammar.title: Polite Requests with 'Poder' and 'Querer'
grammar.explanation:
When ordering at a restaurant or making polite requests, Spanish uses the verbs 'poder' (can) and 'querer' (to want) in the conditional or present tense:

• ¿Puede traerme...? - Can you bring me...?
• ¿Nos puede traer...? - Can you bring us...?
• Quiero / Quisiera... - I want / I would like...
• Me gustaría... - I would like...

The conditional form 'quisiera' or 'me gustaría' is more polite than 'quiero'. Always add 'por favor' for politeness.
